title: Tournament Day
text: Inter-school tournament. Your asso has trained for months, the stands are full of face paint, and the team from the other grande école looks extremely awake. The whistle blows.

choices.label: Give absolutely everything
choices.hint: Glory or a bag of ice

success.text: Health check passed: you win in the last minute. The whole asso carries you to the bus. Someone films it, forever.

failure.text: Health check failed: you lose by a whisker and limp to the bus. The chants on the ride home are still glorious.

choices.label: Play for fun
choices.hint: The third half is the real match

effects.text: You lose cheerfully and win the after-party. Priorities.

title: Ouch
text: A bad landing, a crack you hear more than feel. The physio says 'six weeks, minimum'. The team says 'we need you on Saturday'.

effects.text: Six weeks on the sofa. Your grades enjoy the attention.

success.text: Health check passed: you play, you score, you limp heroically. Legend status unlocked.

failure.text: Health check failed: six weeks become four months. Your knee now forecasts the weather.

title: The Pandemic
text: A new virus brings a new vocabulary: lockdown, cluster, 'you're on mute'. Your flat becomes your office, your gym and your entire social life. Two years lived through a screen. How do you get through it?

footprint.label: Extra screens and streaming during lockdowns

variants.text: A new virus brings a new vocabulary: lockdown, cluster, R number. Overnight, your health-economics team is the most important room in the country, and your models are on the evening news. How do you get through it?

hints: Effects differ by path: health research shines, finance and consulting wobble, Big Tech booms.

effects.text: Your sourdough starter has a name and a better social life than you.
You become an amateur epidemiologist with a minor in panic.
You deliver groceries to the fourth floor. The neighbour there teaches you belote over the phone.

title: The Old Asso Friend
text: Malik, your old asso friend, texts at midnight: 'Coffee? I have a crazy idea and I need a CTO I trust.' The deck has twelve slides, nine of them about the mission. The salary is mostly equity and vibes.
speaker: asso_friend

hints: Reference the asso you were in together (asso_* flag).

success.text: Investor pitch: your Network and Math & AI sold it. Series B. Malik cries on stage. You pretend not to, badly.

failure.text: Investor pitch failed: eighteen months later, the runway ends. You land a corporate strategy job and a great story for dinner parties.

choices.label: Advise on the side
choices.hint: A foot in, a foot out

effects.text: Thursday evenings become startup evenings. Malik pays you in equity and pizza.
You say no over a long dinner. You both check the startup's news for years.

title: The AI Shock
text: In six months, AI goes from 'helpful assistant' to 'does most of what your team does, before lunch'. The headlines say 'historic productivity'. Your company calls an all-hands meeting with no agenda.

variants.text: The AI shock hits {employer} on a Monday. By Friday, your role is 'fully automated'. Security walks you out with a cardboard box and a sympathetic face. The severance is decent. Nobody in your field is hiring humans for it any more.

effects.text: Your job now runs on a server somewhere. Your field won't hire you back.

variants.text: In six months, AI goes from 'helpful assistant' to 'does most of what your team does'. You've used these tools as a sparring partner for years: overnight, you're the person everyone asks for help, and your manager asks for your salary expectations.

In six months, AI goes from 'helpful assistant' to 'does most of what your team does, before lunch'. You keep your job, but your job description is rewritten by the same AI that now does half of it. Your raise is 'postponed'.

hints: If flag COMPLEMENT, callback to the research paper where the player used AI as a sparring partner.
If flag SHALLOW, callback to the research paper that 'wrote itself'.
If the job is lost, be kind: this is a turning point, not a failure.

effects.text: Online courses at 11PM, a study group of forty-year-olds, a certificate you're weirdly proud of.
Your friends don't fix anything. They make everything bearable, which is better.

choices.label: Ride the wave, invest in it

effects.text: You buy shares in the company that automated your colleagues. It goes up. You feel complicated.

title: PM, Again
text: At a conference on AI and society, the keynote speaker walks on stage: white hair now, same energy, same squeaky marker. It's PM. After the talk, PM walks straight towards you.
speaker: pm

variants.text: At a conference on AI and society, the keynote speaker is PM: white hair now, same energy. After the talk PM walks straight to you: 'Front row, every single 8AM. I always knew.' PM wants you on a panel next month.

At a conference on AI and society, the keynote speaker is PM: white hair now, same energy. After the talk PM walks straight to you and squints: 'The empty seat at 8AM. I remember you.' A smile. 'So, what did you do with all that sleep?'

hints: PM remembers the 8AM classes: callback to attendance (pm_regular) or skips (skipped_pm). Only ever 'PM'.

effects.text: One coffee becomes three and eats your whole afternoon. PM still writes on napkins like they're whiteboards.
On stage, PM introduces you as 'a former student, for better or worse'. The room laughs. You do too.
You walk away talking to nobody. PM, unbothered, waves anyway.

title: Your Teenager
text: Your teenager hasn't really slept in weeks. TikTac glows under the duvet at 3AM, and the school nurse used the word 'anxiety' twice in one call. The screens that bought you quiet dinners have sent the bill.
speaker: kid

effects.text: The first week is war. By the third, you're all playing cards at the kitchen table, grumbling happily.
A therapist with excellent plants helps everyone say the things. It takes months. It works.
The phase lasts years. Your kid moves out at eighteen and calls on birthdays.

title: The Document
text: Late one evening, a file lands in your inbox by mistake: what {employer} is really doing with its data, its emissions or its clients. It's bad. It's provable. Nobody knows you've seen it.

variants.text: Late one evening, a file lands in your inbox by mistake: the real client list behind Palantire's 'public safety' contracts. It's bad. It's provable. Nobody knows you've seen it.

Late one evening, a file lands in your inbox by mistake: TotalEnnemies's internal climate models, decades old and very accurate, next to its public statements. It's bad. It's provable. Nobody knows you've seen it.

choices.label: Blow the whistle
choices.hint: The right thing, at a huge price

effects.text: Your name is on the front page for a week and in a parliamentary report for good. Your career, as it was, is over. Something better starts.

success.text: Network check passed: against all odds, the board listens. A program is quietly cancelled. Nobody will ever know it was you.

failure.text: Network check failed: your report disappears into a committee that meets twice a year. You get a 'thank you for your vigilance' email.

effects.text: You empty the trash folder twice. You still dream about it sometimes.

title: War, Energy, Minerals
text: A war far away turns out to be closer than it looks. Gas prices triple, chip factories pause, and your electricity bill arrives with a warning label. The news is a wall of maps with arrows.

variants.text: A war far away turns out to be closer than it looks, and your phone rings at 4AM: the ceasefire talks need someone who understands energy and AI. Gas prices triple, chip factories pause. Everyone is looking at your team.

effects.text: Nineteen degrees in the living room and a very fashionable collection of jumpers.
A family of four stays for eight months. Your kitchen learns new spices; your heart learns new words.

choices.label: Stock up and refresh the news

effects.text: Forty kilos of pasta and a news app on every screen. It doesn't help, but it feels like doing something.

success.text: Economics check passed: you call the energy spike right. Your bonus is excellent. Your dinner-party stories are not.

failure.text: Economics check failed: you call it wrong, twice. The desk calls it 'a learning experience'.

title: Heatwave Summer
text: It's 43 °C in July, again. The tram rails buckle, the river is a trickle, and your doctor hands you a leaflet titled 'Surviving summer after 65'. The weather map has a new colour for this.

variants.text: It's 43 °C in July, again. The tram rails buckle and the river is a trickle, but your insulated walls and shutters keep the flat bearable. Half the street knocks on your door to sit in your cool room.

ai.tone: the planet hits back, but stay human and warm
hints: This only fires when the player's projected 2100 temperature is high: hint that their lifestyle, multiplied by everyone, made these summers.

effects.text: You spend August in the dark with a wet towel on your neck, listening to the radio count the days.

footprint.label: Air conditioning in heatwave summers (design estimate)

effects.text: Your flat is a fridge. The street outside is two degrees hotter because of everyone's fridges.

choices.label: Open a cool room for neighbours

effects.text: Every afternoon, the old man from the sixth floor brings cards and the kid from the second brings ice lollies.

title: Battery at 1%
text: One Tuesday you sit in your car outside the office and simply cannot go in. Your body has filed the resignation your mind refused to write. The doctor's note says one word, and gives you a year to find yourself again.

ai.tone: warm, gently funny, never mocking the burnout itself
hints: Reference the work rhythm choice (grind) if relevant.
End on a note of hope: this is a pause, not an ending.

choices.label: Take the year. Really take it.

effects.text: You sleep for a month, walk for a season, and slowly remember what you liked about mornings.

choices.label: A month with goats in Brittany

effects.text: Thirty goats, zero notifications. One of them eats your badge. You come back slower, browner, and strangely wise about cheese.

choices.label: Rest, then back to the grind

effects.text: You go back at full speed. Your calendar welcomes you like nothing happened. Your body keeps the receipt.
You come back four days a week with a new rule: no Slacker after 7PM. The company survives. So do you.

title: The Scandal
text: A journalist calls. Then another. Leaked documents show what your work at {employer} was really used for, and your name is in paragraph three. Your phone has 214 notifications and none of them are friends.

hints: Tie the scandal to {employer} and what it does (surveillance, oil, finance, social media). Use only the game's parody names, never a real company.

effects.text: You publish a long, honest LinkedOut post. Half the internet calls you brave, the other half calls you late. Both are right.
Your lawyers write a statement with the word 'regrettable' four times. It works, legally.

choices.label: Leak the rest yourself
choices.hint: If it's coming out, all of it

effects.text: You hand the journalist the full archive. The story changes overnight: from accomplice to source.

title: It's Not Just a Habit
text: What started as 'just Thursdays' has quietly taken over your weeks. You've cancelled plans to keep the habit fed, and your mornings start with shaking hands. Someone who loves you finally says it out loud.

effects.text: A doctor, a group on Tuesdays, a friend on speed dial. Day by day, it loosens its grip.

success.text: Willpower check passed (Health): it's harder than you thought and you do it anyway.

failure.text: Willpower check failed: three weeks clean, then a bad Friday. Back to square one.

effects.text: You change the subject. Your friend stops bringing it up. That's worse.

title: Quiet Evenings
text: Another Friday night with a ready meal and a muted TV. Your phone has notifications from Slacker and from the bank, but nobody has called just to call in weeks. The silence has started to feel heavy.

ai.tone: gentle, melancholic, hopeful at the end

effects.text: Your oldest friend from AIDAMS picks up on the second ring: 'Finally!' You talk for two hours.

choices.label: Join a choir or a club

effects.text: You can't sing. Nobody cares. Wednesday becomes your favourite day.
You answer emails at midnight. The inbox, at least, always replies.

title: The Big Exit
text: The acquisition closes on a Thursday. Your bank calls to check the transfer isn't a mistake. For the first time in your life, the question isn't 'can I afford it?' but 'what on earth do I do with all this?'

ai.tone: absurd luxury satire, BitLife energy, never preachy
hints: Name the startup if known. Every option is fun; the end receipt will show the yacht.

footprint.label: Your yacht's fuel and crew flights (design estimate)

effects.text: Her name is 'Exit Strategy'. She burns more fuel in a weekend than your car did in a decade, and the photos are spectacular.

footprint.label: Suborbital space-tourism flight (design estimate, incl. soot)

effects.text: Eleven minutes, four of them weightless. You see the thin blue line of the atmosphere and, for a second, understand everything.

footprint.label: Running a vineyard (machinery, bottles, design estimate)

effects.text: Your first vintage is 'bold, with notes of hubris'. Your second is genuinely good. The vines don't care about your exit multiple.
Your mum cries, your dad pretends to inspect the gutters. The guest room has your name on the door.

success.text: Network check passed: nine fail beautifully. The tenth becomes a unicorn. You are now 'a legendary early investor' on panels.

failure.text: Network check failed: all ten fail, gracefully. Your friends are grateful forever. You have very good seats at ten weddings.

effects.text: Forty schoolyards get a tiny dense forest. In ten years, kids will play in the shade on 40 °C days and never know your name.

title: The Grandchild's Video
text: Your grandchild wants to film you explaining 'how life was before AI' for TikTac. 'It could go viral.' You have opinions, a good jumper and nothing left to lose.

variants.text: Your neighbour's grandchild wants to film you explaining 'how life was before AI' for TikTac. 'It could go viral.' You have opinions, a good jumper and nothing left to lose.

success.text: Four million views. Teenagers worldwide now say 'back in my day, we had to think' in your voice.

failure.text: Two hundred views, mostly family. Your sister comments 'iconic'.

effects.text: You both go to the park instead. The best video is the one nobody filmed.

choices.label: Teach them to fix a laptop

effects.text: You revive a twelve-year-old laptop together. It boots. You both cheer like it's a moon landing.

title: The Talk
text: Your partner sits you down on a Sunday evening, the bad kind of calm. 'We need to talk about us.' The dishwasher hums. Somewhere a neighbour is practising the trumpet, badly.
speaker: partner

hints: Charisma check on couples therapy. If flag met_3am, callback to the 3AM night they met.

success.text: Reconciliation: your Charisma and a very patient therapist saved it. You're better at talking than you were at thirty.

failure.text: Therapy check failed: you both try, honestly, and it isn't enough. You separate as kindly as two people can.

effects.text: Two flats, two sets of keys, and a shared calendar for everything that still matters.
You hit every deadline that year. Your partner moves out in March. You notice in April.
